meta.title: LINKEON.IO — an AI team for your business
meta.description: AI assistants (marketer, lawyer, accountant, career counsellor, coach) plus one shared profile. For small businesses, freelancers and agencies.

business.text: A contract, the taxes, the email that should have gone out yesterday. A lawyer, an accountant and a marketer — without hiring anyone, without booking an appointment.

problem.h2: More to do than one person can carry

items.title: The small stuff takes the day
items.text: Reply to a client, finish the post, give the contract a read. By evening you've done plenty, and the thing it was all for hasn't moved.

items.title: No one to ask
items.text: A five-minute question, and no one to put it to: the lawyer is busy, the accountant will get back to you tomorrow, and it has to be settled now.

items.title: Explaining yourself from scratch every time
items.text: Ten tabs and ten services, and in every one of them you start over: who you are and what you do.

problem.footer: Linkeon brings this into one place: the assistants do the work, and what you said once, they all remember.

agentic.h2: Your assistant doesn't reply with text — it does the work
agentic.sub: A regular bot can only write back. A Linkeon assistant has a workspace of its own: it opens your files, searches the web, writes and runs code, puts a document together — and hands you the finished file.
agentic.note: Files are processed on Linkeon's side — nothing to install on your computer. Runs on the same tokens as the conversation.

faq.h2: What to know before you start

items.q: What are tokens and how are they spent?
items.a: Tokens are the internal currency. They're used for each assistant reply, generated image or second of video. They don't expire.

Sign in with Yandex, Google or your phone number — 2 minutes. You start with 25,000 tokens on the house: roughly 7 assistant replies or 5 images. That won't get you far with video — for that you'll need a pack.
Yes. Only you have access to your profile. In settings you control what assistants remember.

items.q: Can I cancel a token purchase?
items.a: Tokens never expire, so a purchase has no deadline — but we don't refund an unused balance. We do refund money in two cases: the service was down for more than 72 hours straight, or you were charged twice. Email support@linkeon.io — we review it within 10 business days.
Not yet. We're working on it — ping support if you're interested, we'll speed things up.

items.q: How is it different from ChatGPT?
items.a: ChatGPT is one helper. Linkeon is a team of assistants with a shared profile + image and video generation in one bill.

items.q: How much does a website or bot cost?
items.a: Creating one is free, and so is the first month. After that it's {{tokens}} tokens a month for each. Changes are charged separately, by the amount of work — like assistant replies. If you run out of tokens, the site goes to sleep: code, address and domain are kept, and it wakes up by itself once you top up. No debt builds up. Each account can have up to two websites or bots; if you need more, write to support.

items.q: Can I connect my own domain?
items.a: Yes, for free — it's included in the rent. Enter the domain on the website's card: Linkeon shows which records to create at your registrar, checks them itself and issues the certificate. The Linkeon address keeps working alongside. Only a website can have its own domain; a bot has no address.

items.q: What if a change breaks the site?
items.a: After every change, Linkeon checks that the site opens. If it doesn't, Linkeon rolls back to the previous version by itself, and no tokens are charged for that change. Any change from the history can also be undone by hand — with one click.
